content: Fleet integration standard: use Bun package/runtime scripts and TSGo (`tsgo`) for TypeScript checks across OpenCode plugin fleet. `opencode-fleet` owns manifest/install/doctor/test/hygiene/telemetry CLI; Conductor owns doctrine/profile/policy; Engram is the local telemetry/memory sink; Concord remains disabled in local config until explicitly enabled and owns live edit coordination; Codemem owns graph/drift/review focus. `opencode-fleet hygiene` now flags non-Bun lockfiles, tsc script references, and direct `typescript` devDependencies.

Concord+Codemem review: Concord has strong automated mock/real-daemon/Rust validation and existing TS/Rust benchmark harnesses, but repeatable live/manual validation is under-specified and docs/CI still have npm drift. Codemem has strong verify pipeline with TSGo/Bun/Cargo and agent-facing graph tools, but no real packaged OpenCode+daemon smoke and no benchmark suite; performance targets are documented in docs/init.md but not enforced. Integration path: Conductor should ingest Concord collisions as lifecycle artifacts/spine events, Engram should add lifecycle/concord artifact kinds and correlation-aware context requests, Fleet telemetry should gain correlation_id/spine_seq/concord_event_id/source_refs, and subagent runs should get structured IDs/status docs tied to plan/wave/tool calls.

Executed first Concord/Engram/Conductor correlation integration wave. Concord rejected acquire responses now carry optional `eventId` and `guidanceXml`; the plugin attaches machine-readable `concord` metadata to thrown errors while preserving XML guidance messages. Conductor now exposes `run_init` for structured subagent run records and `lifecycle_concord_ingest` to import `concord collisions --json`, write `.opencode/lifecycle/artifacts/concord/<event>.json|xml`, append `concord.collision.detected` spine events, and checkpoint ingestion. Engram now discovers lifecycle/concord artifacts and accepts correlation-aware context signals. Fleet telemetry schema now includes correlation/plan/wave/agent/tool/spine/concord/source refs. Codemem now has an initial Bun benchmark harness (`bun run bench -- --quick`) and README tool list updated.

Continuation wave: added repeatable runtime validation. Concord now has `bun run live-smoke` (`scripts/live-smoke.ts`) that builds TS/debug daemon, uses the real plugin+daemon path in a temp /tmp worktree, verifies disjoint hunk locks, overlap rejection, machine-readable eventId, daemon health, and collision event query. Codemem now has `bun run smoke:packaged` (`scripts/smoke-packaged.ts`) that installs local tgz artifacts in a temp config, verifies the packaged `codemem` bin, and runs `doctor` + `check`; `bun run bench -- --quick` remains executable. Fleet manifest now uses Codemem `check_command: bun run verify && bun run smoke:packaged`; Concord has a future `check_command: bun run check && bun run live-smoke -- --json` but remains disabled. Conductor docs now document Concord -> lifecycle artifacts -> Engram context flow.

Benchmark continuation wave: Concord now has `bun run bench:threshold` via `scripts/bench-threshold.ts`, rerunning TS IPC/lock-model benches and failing on local p95/p99 thresholds; TS bench scripts create `bench/results` before writing. Codemem `scripts/bench.ts` now has quick mode plus full synthetic-project mode measuring cold status, cold check, hot-edit check, review-focus, and warm status; package adds `bench:quick`. Fleet manifests wire Codemem enabled validation to `bun run verify && bun run smoke:packaged && bun run bench:quick`; Concord disabled future validation now includes `bun run bench:threshold`.

Continuation wave: opencode-fleet now supports `test --include-disabled [name|all]` for on-demand validation of disabled plugins. Config adds `fleet:test:concord`, which ran Concord's disabled check command (`bun run check && bun run live-smoke -- --json && bun run bench:threshold`) through Fleet without enabling Concord in daily OpenCode config. Codemem now has `bench:threshold` with quick/full modes and writes benchmark reports under `bench/results/` (ignored). Conductor `run_init` now writes a compact `.opencode/status/run-<id>.json` mirror alongside `.opencode/runs/run_<id>.json` to correlate agent_run_id/correlation_id/workspace_id with existing status tooling.

Persisted final plan `fleet-correlation` (8 waves, 56 tasks) for OpenCode plugin fleet full implementation. Key architectural decisions locked: (1) new shared package `@jackmazac/opencode-fleet-contracts` owns IDs/telemetry/artifact/health schemas — NOT grafted onto host-adapter; (2) keep both `plan_id` (ULID) and `plan_slug` with `.opencode/plans/index.json` mapping; (3) ULID via `ulid` npm (Engram already uses); (4) canonical `FleetTelemetryEnvelope` with all correlation IDs nullable, schema_version:1, ISO 8601 ts; (5) canonical `HealthReport` shape normalizes Fleet's `pass`→`ok`; (6) Engram correlation via additive sidecar table `chunk_correlation` — never widen hot write path; (7) `explore_fast` stays in Conductor (Cursor-CLI agent exploration ≠ Codemem code-graph truth); (8) `opencode.json` generated via Fleet W6.4 with sibling `.opencode-fleet.lock.json` (JSON forbids comments); user sections preserved; (9) Fleet `install` runs `bun install` with `--frozen-lockfile` when present + `--dry-run` shield + backups; (10) Concord re-enable is last flag flip, gated on W4+W6 green. Full plan body at `/var/folders/ml/p_w___pn5jlbtt8fj2lrvwbm0000gp/T/opencode/fleet-plan/plan.md`. 8 user decisions pending confirmation before execution: publish contracts pkg, telemetry export, auto `bun install`, opencode.json generation, plan_id backfill, Concord re-enable, context_usage move, global .opencode/ deletion.
